external_entities.name: supplier
external_entities.description: A supplier that uploads compliance paperwork and signs in to the supplier document portal.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Suppliers upload their compliance paperwork through a portal

external_entities.name: category manager
external_entities.description: A category manager who reviews uploaded paperwork and approves or rejects it.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network, review what has been uploaded and approve or reject it.

external_entities.name: vendor
external_entities.description: The vendor that hosts the portal and pushes nightly supplier data extracts.
external_entities.source_excerpt: The vendor hosts it and we do not run any part of it.

processes.name: supplier document portal
processes.description: A vendor-hosted SaaS portal through which suppliers upload paperwork and category managers review and approve or reject it.
processes.notes: The vendor datasheet says the platform is secure by design, that it uses enterprise-grade encryption throughout, that all access is fully authenticated and audited, and that the product is fully compliant.

processes.name: supplier master service
processes.description: A service that loads the nightly supplier data extract and writes records into the supplier database.
processes.source_excerpt: Our supplier master service loads that file and writes the records into the supplier database.

data_stores.name: vendor platform
data_stores.description: The vendor platform where the compliance documents remain.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The documents themselves stay in the vendor's platform.

data_stores.name: landing bucket
data_stores.description: A bucket in the organisation's cloud account that receives the nightly supplier data extract.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Every night the vendor pushes a supplier data extract to a landing bucket in our cloud account.
data_stores.notes: The runbook says the file arrives as a plain CSV and is picked up as-is.

data_stores.name: supplier database
data_stores.description: The supplier database into which the supplier master service writes extracted records.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The bucket, the service and the database are all in our cloud account.

data_flows.name: upload compliance paperwork
data_flows.description: A supplier uploads compliance paperwork to the portal.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Suppliers upload their compliance paperwork through a portal
data_flows.data_description: insurance certificates, food safety audits, and contact details for suppliers' staff

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: A supplier signs in to the portal.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Suppliers sign in with a username and password that the vendor issues to them.

data_flows.name: review and approve paperwork
data_flows.description: A category manager reviews uploaded paperwork and approves or rejects it.
data_flows.source_excerpt: review what has been uploaded and approve or reject it

data_flows.name: store compliance documents
data_flows.description: The portal stores uploaded compliance documents in the vendor platform.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The documents themselves stay in the vendor's platform.
data_flows.data_description: compliance paperwork and staff contact details

data_flows.name: push supplier data extract
data_flows.description: The vendor pushes a nightly supplier data extract to the landing bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every night the vendor pushes a supplier data extract to a landing bucket in our cloud account.
data_flows.notes: Conflicting claims: System description says "We were told the nightly extract is encrypted end to end." The runbook says "the file arrives as a plain CSV and is picked up as-is."

data_flows.name: load supplier data extract
data_flows.description: The supplier master service loads the nightly extract from the landing bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Our supplier master service loads that file

data_flows.name: write supplier records
data_flows.description: The supplier master service writes extracted records into the supplier database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: writes the records into the supplier database

trust_boundaries.name: vendor hosting
trust_boundaries.description: The vendor-controlled hosting environment for the SaaS portal and vendor platform.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The vendor hosts it and we do not run any part of it.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network from which category managers work.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network

trust_boundaries.name: our cloud account
trust_boundaries.description: The organisation's cloud account containing the landing bucket, supplier master service, and supplier database.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The bucket, the service and the database are all in our cloud account.

assumptions.assumption: The vendor platform's stated enterprise-grade encryption throughout includes encryption at rest.
assumptions.basis: The vendor datasheet says the platform uses "enterprise-grade encryption throughout" and the documents stay in the vendor platform.

assumptions.assumption: The compliance paperwork and staff contact details are confidential because they contain personal and commercially sensitive information.
assumptions.basis: The vendor platform stores insurance certificates, food safety audits, and contact details for suppliers' staff.

assumptions.assumption: The landing bucket contents are confidential because it stores the supplier data extract containing supplier records and staff contact details.
assumptions.basis: The landing bucket receives the nightly supplier data extract.

assumptions.assumption: The supplier database contents are confidential because it stores supplier records derived from the supplier data extract.
assumptions.basis: The supplier master service writes supplier records into the supplier database.
